issues: The source does not expressly state that every included current or subsequently approved formulation/strength/concentration/delivery mechanism must independently be marketed in the US. The program imposes is_marketed_in_us=true on every variant, which is a plausible interpretation but not an exact stated exception or condition.

The source identifies the listed drug as having both stated NDC numbers; the program converts this into an either-NDC condition. That may be commercially sensible for distinct package presentations, but the source does not expressly state that either NDC alone is sufficient.

Case out_variant_but_not_fda is internally incompatible with the source framing: it stipulates a current or subsequently approved MOXATAG variant while denying FDA approval. The inclusion expressly concerns approved formulations, and the definition's identified approval authority is the FDA.

No authoritative FDA/NDC/marketing records or time anchor are supplied for the external, time-dependent facts invoked by the definition, especially 'currently and subsequently approved.' The quoted definition alone cannot establish actual variant status or US marketing status.
The source defines PARTY by identity: each of T&L and Igene. It does not impose an exact-string, capitalization-sensitive entity_name matching rule.

The predicate unsupportedly treats spelling, capitalization, punctuation, and corporate-suffix variants as necessarily distinct non-PARTY entities. The source provides no alias, legal-name, or identity-resolution rule establishing those exclusions.
Several exclusion cases state only that a label is not an exact textual match; that does not establish that the underlying entity is not T&L or Igene under the contractual definition.
Use an entity-identity field or an explicitly sourced canonical-name/alias rule rather than exact equality on an entity_name label.

The source requires an agreement that Cisco entered into and under which Cisco authorizes particular resellers. The predicate substitutes the non-identical condition `authorizing_party_is_cisco`; being described as the authorizing party does not expressly establish that Cisco entered into the agreement, so this is not an exact implementation of the quoted condition.

case_05 codes both authorization fields true, but its text says only that the agreement authorizes unspecified 'particular resellers' and expressly says Elliot is not a party. It does not explicitly state that Elliot is among the authorized resellers or that the agreement authorizes Elliot's purchase and resale.

The source defines a Help Desk as a physical location within the head office that is "designated as an immediate contact point to provide service assistance to customers." The proposed predicate replaces the designation's stated purpose with a separate, stronger factual condition that the location actually "provides service assistance to customers." Actual provision is not expressly required by the quoted definition.

The source does not independently state four conjunctive criteria; the service-assistance language grammatically qualifies the designation as an immediate contact point. Treating it as a separately testable operational fact is a non-exact gloss.

Case in_kfda_agency states only a disjunction—Korean Food and Drug Administration or a successor agency thereto—but codes the specific fact entity_type=Korean Food and Drug Administration. The text does not establish that specific branch.

Case out_mfds identifies the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety but does not state that it is not a successor agency to the Korean Food and Drug Administration. Because successor status is an expressly required factual determination, coding it as an excluded entity type is unsupported by the case text.
The predicate itself correctly implements the quoted definition: KFDA includes the Korean Food and Drug Administration and any successor agency thereto.

The quoted definition incorporates the externally defined term "Governmental Authority," but no definition or attachment for that term is provided. The program can test an asserted governmental-authority status, but the source package is insufficient to determine that status from underlying facts or to audit its full scope.
The predicate faithfully includes exactly the expressly enumerated places plus all U.S. territories, possessions, and U.S. military bases; it does not add an unsupported exception.

Case canada codes location_status as foreign_state, but its text identifies Ontario as a province of Canada. A province is not explicitly a foreign state, so the coded fact does not match the stated fact text.
The source quote and supplied case descriptions are sufficient; no required attachment or redacted determinative fact is identified.

The foreign-entity provision is not exactly represented. It depends on the applicable legal maximum ownership percentage for the foreign investor and on the ownership condition as modified by that maximum; the single value foreign_lower_with_power does not encode the legally permitted maximum or establish that the relevant ownership threshold is met.

The foreign provision also does not create a substitute independent control basis in the way modeled: possession of power to direct management or policies is already independently sufficient under clause (a).

c4's foreign-investor facts concern the investor's control of Person D, rather than the stated direct control by D of Party X. Thus its coded control_basis does not explicitly support the relevant D-to-Party control relationship.

c9 expressly states that Person I indirectly controls Party X, but the program rejects it solely because an external foreign investor lacks power to direct I. That fact does not negate I's stated control of Party X under the definition.

c10 explicitly states that Person J controls Party X through power to direct management, which is direct control under the source. Coding connection_type as none causes an erroneous rejection and conflicts with the text.

c14 does not state that Party X controls the intermediary or otherwise has the intermediary's contractual power; an intermediary's power over Person N alone does not establish X's indirect control of N.

Definitions of Party and Person, expressly listed as dependencies, are not supplied. The external-law facts needed to apply the foreign-ownership proviso are also unavailable beyond case-specific assertions.

The predicate applies candidate_is_other_person=true to every alternative, including the separate director/officer/employee alternative. The quoted definition limits the 'any other Person' wording to the controlling/controlled/common-control clause; its distinct '(2) any director, officer or employee' clause does not expressly impose that qualifier. This added gate is not an exact reflection of the text.

The definition of 'Person' is referenced but not supplied. Because the proposed predicate and several cases depend on whether Given and Candidate are Persons, the source package is insufficient to validate that term or classifications involving non-Persons.

No case tests the consequential omitted scenario: a director, officer, or employee of the given Person who does not satisfy candidate_is_other_person. Therefore the case set does not expose the predicate's added restriction.

The source separately includes a company that is "owned ... by" CERES and a company "controlled by" CERES. The proposed predicate treats ownership only as the defined control test of more than 50% voting stock/shares, thereby omitting direct ownership by CERES at 50% or less.
The source's definition of "control" supplies the more-than-50% ownership and director-nomination tests for control; it does not state that those thresholds restrict the separate "owned by" limb.

The listed fatal cases expressly state direct CERES ownership at exactly 50%, 40%, and 10%, respectively, but the proposed predicate returns false because none exceeds 50% and no other control condition is present.

The source's phrase "transfer by operation of law or otherwise" is open-ended. The predicate limits action_type to a finite enumerated set and excludes a stated lease, rather than capturing any other transfer of a listed subject matter. A lease may qualify as a transfer 'otherwise' depending on its legal effect, so a categorical exclusion of leases is not an exact implementation.

The provided source quote depends on externally defined terms, including "you," "Agreement," "material portion," "interest," and "assets." Those definitions are identified as dependencies but are not supplied, so the complete contract rule cannot be verified or applied without the missing attachments/definitions.

The lease case states that a lease occurs but does not state whether that lease constitutes an 'otherwise' transfer under the governing contract or applicable definition. Its exclusion cannot be validated from the supplied facts and quote alone.

The predicate accurately implements the stated definition: qualifying matter must be words, symbols, photographic representations, graphic representations, or combinations thereof, and must identify Manning. The 'such as' name-and-likeness language is correctly not treated as an exclusive requirement.

The supplied excerpt does not identify which person 'Manning' denotes. Several examples specifically assert Peyton Manning, which requires external contractual context or an identity attachment not included in the source excerpt.

The predicate exactly implements the quoted definition: non-ownership, memo, bailee status, and consignment absent an otherwise agreement by the applicable consignor are alternative grounds for exclusion.
Each case text expressly states every coded Boolean fact and matches its fact vector.

The definition of "Merchant" is identified as a dependency but is not supplied. This prevents confirmation of the term's contractual scope, although it does not alter the logical structure of the quoted Excluded Goods definition.

The source says "flash data storage" whereas the predicate substitutes "flash data storage product." The excerpt does not explicitly establish that these are identical terms, so this is a plausible but not exact normalization.

The inclusive disjunction is correctly represented by the predicate, but the first predicate field should preserve the source terminology or be supported by a definition equating flash data storage with flash data storage products.

The source requires that the benefit relationship be "pursuant to" the relevant contract. The predicate has no contract-nexus field or condition and therefore treats any qualifying contract plus independent benefit relationships as sufficient.

Each purported in-scope case states that a contract exists and that the relevant parties provide or receive a benefit involving a third party, but none explicitly states that those benefits are provided or received pursuant to that contract. Consequently, those cases do not establish the source definition's required nexus.

The standalone third_party_involved condition is redundant if the benefit-relation field is true, because that field already expressly requires a benefit to or from a third party. It is not itself a source-independent eligibility requirement.
Conditioned on the supplied Boolean status facts, the predicate exactly implements: a Person excluding SutroVax, Sutro, and an Affiliate of either respective entity.
Each case's fact vector matches its stated fact text, including explicit negative facts.

The supplied source excerpt does not include the operative definitions or source support for the capitalized/dependent concepts Person and Affiliates, nor source material establishing the relevant identities/statuses of SutroVax and Sutro. These omissions prevent verification that the asserted case statuses use the contract meanings of those terms.

The source does not require an instrument to be an 'original tariff' in order to qualify. It covers intrastate and/or interstate tariffs, while also including supplements and reissues. In out_other_instrument, the text expressly states that the instrument is an intrastate tariff and satisfies every stated substantive condition; its being neither an original tariff, supplement, nor reissue does not defeat coverage under the source. The predicate improperly imposes a closed instrument_nature taxonomy and excludes qualifying tariffs classified as 'other'.

The predicate faithfully implements the source as a disjunction of each enumerated Person category. The parenthetical confirms that an other form of business organization qualifies whether or not it is a legal entity; it does not add a required fact omitted from the predicate.

Multiple case vectors assert negative classifications that the corresponding fact text does not expressly state. For example, stating that an item is a partnership, corporation, LLC, joint venture, association, or trust does not explicitly establish that it is not also an association, other business organization, or other entity or organization under the broad contractual wording.

c07 states that the sole proprietorship is an unlisted business organization, but does not expressly establish every remaining negative-coded field, particularly is_other_entity_or_organization=false.

c09 and c10 state only that the subjects are organizations, while coding them as other entities or organizations and coding every named category false. The text should expressly state the intended residual classification and exclusions.

The nonentity examples c11-c15 are generally textually adequate as negative examples because they expressly describe objects as not entities or organizations; c01 expressly states exclusive individual classification.

The predicate impermissibly treats a utility patent, design patent, utility model, or inventor's certificate as independently sufficient even when not an issued patent. The quoted definition instead describes 'any issued patent, including' those types; it does not expressly include an unissued listed type merely because it has that label.

The exception field reverses or at least materially distorts the source language. The source says Patent Applications are included 'unless the context otherwise requires'; it does not say they are excluded where context requires treating them 'as a patent.' A context requiring treatment as a patent would support, rather than defeat, inclusion.

The fact text and vectors for patent_application_context_override and unissued_application_context_override are internally contradictory: their descriptions say the context requires treating the application as not a patent, while their explicit coded-fact sentence says the context requires treating it as a patent.

The EPO and foreign-equivalent cases code is_like_governmental_grant_or_registration_for_inventions as false despite the quoted definition expressly including patents granted by the EPO and foreign equivalents in its governmental-grant/registration language. At minimum, the source does not support coding those facts as false.

The source is not sufficient to resolve the stated dependencies: 'Patent Application' is defined elsewhere, and the source supplies no standards or attachments for determining a 'like' governmental grant, a foreign equivalent, or when context otherwise requires a different result.

The case set asserts legal-status facts such as non-issued listed utility models/certificates and foreign equivalence without source support establishing that those statuses are compatible with or excluded by the quoted definition.

The amendment/replacement/successor clause is not an alternative Applicable Law definition with an independent applicability requirement. It provides that specific references to an Applicable Law or portion thereof include its amendments, replacements, and successors. The proposed predicate instead classifies any such item as Applicable Law only if separately applicable to Party activities.

Case_09 exposes the error: the source's inclusion of successors is unconditional once a reference is to the Applicable Law, whereas the predicate returns false solely because the successor is coded as not independently applicable to Party activities.

The source does not define the capitalized term "Regulatory Approvals." Its inclusion as a separately coded instrument category therefore depends on an absent external contract definition, although the source does establish that Regulatory Approvals are included within permits.
